- When sentiment is high (≥0.7), model tends to underpredict; increase forecast slightly to align with bullish momentum.  
- When sentiment is low (≤0.5), model overpredicts; reduce forecast to reflect bearish bias.  
- Model consistently underestimates late-period spikes (especially 28–30d); add 2–5% buffer for final 5–7 days if sentiment is rising.  
- Model often overshoots early in the 30d horizon after a spike; cap forecast at 10–15% above recent peak if sentiment is neutral or slightly bullish.  
- Mean reversion bias: if 30d forecast is 5%+ above 18d history mean, reduce by 1–2% unless sentiment is strongly bullish.  
- Horizon-specific: 30d forecasts are too conservative in early days (1–7d); add 1–3% to early forecast if sentiment is rising.
